message.content: {"mechanism_id":"seed_conditioned_memory_perturbation","target_component":"F/CR memory adaptation (M_F, M_CR)","observed_evidence":{"task_id":"TASK-05","trace_path":"none_provided","function":"F11","seed":11,"metric":"diversity","observed_value":0.175},"causal_hypothesis":"Seeds 22/33 collapse because early F/CR memory updates lock onto low-diversity settings, while seed 11's memory retains higher F, sustaining diversity; seed sensitivity stems from memory initialization and early Lehmer-mean lock-in.","algorithmic_change":"At each generation, if population diversity (mean pairwise distance normalized by domain) falls below a threshold, inject a seed-derived deterministic perturbation into M_F and M_CR by resampling from their prior distributions, scaled by a decay factor, so collapsed runs re-explore without random restarts.","mathematical_rule":"div_t = mean(||pop_i - pop_j||) / (ub - lb); if div_t < tau: M_F[k] = M_F[k] + alpha * (Cauchy(M_F0, 0.1) - M_F[k]); M_CR[k] = M_CR[k] + alpha * (Normal(M_CR0, 0.1) - M_CR[k]); alpha = 0.5 * exp(-t / T)","expected_effect":"Collapsed seeds (22/33) recover diversity above tau, reducing cross-seed variance in success_rate and final fitness on F11 while leaving seed 11 behavior largely unchanged.","failure_prediction":"If tau is too high, perturbation fires every generation, degrading convergence on easy functions; if alpha too small, collapsed seeds never escape.","ablation_plan":"Compare (a) full mechanism, (b) perturbation without decay (alpha constant), (c) tau=0 (disabled), across seeds 11/22/33 on F11, measuring diversity, success_rate, and final fitness variance.","nearest_known_methods":"Restart strategies, F/CR memory reset heuristics, diversity-triggered parameter resampling in jDE/SHADE variants.","implementation_requirements":"Track normalized pairwise diversity each generation; store prior means M_F0=0.5, M_CR0=0.5; add tau and alpha decay parameters; apply perturbation before mutation sampling."}
